facts.claim: Quintana Roo's lodging tax (Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje, art. 8) is 5% of the invoiced value of lodging at hotels and similar establishments, and 6% for apartments, houses and private villas; the guest who pays for the lodging is the taxpayer (art. 7).

sources.title: Quintana Roo Congress: Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje (consolidated text, last reform 23 Dec 2022)

The state law makes the guest the taxpayer

facts.claim: The law requires the provider to determine, withhold and pay the lodging tax expressly and separately (art. 11); the tax is never part of the value of the lodging (art. 12); on packages that include food and other services, the base is the lodging element, and at least 60% of the invoice total if the invoice does not itemise (art. 10).

facts.claim: Mexico City's Código Fiscal (arts. 162 to 164) taxes lodging: hotels, hostels and motels apply 3.5% to the total value of the lodging consideration (art. 164); where an intermediary collects payment for flats and houses the rate is 5%; the provider is the taxpayer but must pass the tax on to the guest (art. 162).

sources.title: Secretaría de Administración y Finanzas CDMX: Código Fiscal, Del Impuesto por la Prestación de Servicios de Hospedaje (transparency copy, created April 2024)

requires it to pass the tax on to the guest

facts.claim: Article 163: the tax arises when payment is received and the base includes deposits, advances and other concepts; if lodging is bundled with accessory services (transport, food, use of facilities) that the provider does not itemise and prove, the whole value is treated as lodging. The December 2025 decree reforming the Código Fiscal for 2026 changed the audit (dictamen) threshold for lodging-tax payers to 14,913,178 pesos but did not amend arts. 162 to 164. We could not load a consolidated 2026 text.
